notes:
Docket 1.3.79

**Docket runs on macOS 12 again.**

Docket says it needs macOS 12 or later. On 1.3.78, that was not true of the
part that does the work. The app's window opened, but the audit engine inside
it was built in a way that asked macOS for two system functions that only exist
from macOS 13. On macOS 12 the engine could not start, so the app sat there
unable to audit anything, with no clear reason why.

If you are on macOS 12 and Docket opened but never ran an audit, this is the
fix. The engine is now built for macOS 12 on purpose, and every release is
checked, file by file, against the system functions macOS 12 actually has.
A build that fails that check can no longer be published.

**Three findings that were wrong about correct pages.**

We found all three by running Docket on its own website.

- *"No HSTS header"* on sites whose domain ending is already locked to HTTPS.
  Every major browser forces the whole of some domain endings — `.app` and
  `.dev` among them — onto HTTPS before your site is ever asked, so the header
  cannot add anything there. Docket now says so, and says why other
  scorecards will still flag it.
- *"Q&A content with no FAQ markup"* on blog and article index pages. A list of
  posts titled as questions, each linking to the post that answers it, is not
  a set of questions answered on that page, and marking it up as one breaks
  Google's rules for that markup. Index pages are no longer told to.
- *"Hard to read"* on pages built from headings, lists and tables. Docket was
  running each heading or list item into the sentence after it, so a catalogue
  of short titles read as one enormous sentence. It now measures sentences
  only where there are sentences. Pages of long prose are measured as before.

99 checks across 13 areas.
